title: Quantum orientation, Noether structure, composition of systems and operations
abstract: In this paper we argue that, in addition to the statistical structure of quantum theory, another structure, referred to here as the ``Noether structure," is necessary to describe the composition of systems and to define completely positive operations. A Noether structure reflects the dual role of Hermitian operators as observables on the one hand and as generators of symmetry transformations on the other. This idea has been expressed in a similar form in the works of Alfsen and Shultz, who investigated the conditions under which the Jordan product can be extended to an associative product of operator algebras. Our investigations into the Noether structure and the composition of systems are limited to the finite-dimensional case and establish a connection to completely positive operations. In the case of pure operations, the latter can be characterized as orientation-preserving maps.
summary: This theoretical paper proposes that describing composite quantum systems requires a 'Noether structure' beyond the standard statistical axioms. The authors demonstrate that this structure is necessary because simple tensor product rules lead to non-unique mathematical descriptions of combined states and operations. Ultimately, they establish that physical reality must select one specific 'quantum orientation' from multiple mathematically possible choices.
main_problem: The paper argues that quantum theory requires an additional 'Noether structure' beyond its statistical framework to properly describe system composition and define completely positive operations.
main_result: The standard statistical structure for composite systems is not unique, requiring the specification of a 'quantum orientation' (a choice between two possible structures) to fully characterize physical reality.
method: The analysis uses axiomatic approaches, comparing the statistical structure $\langle K, L, \mu angle$ with requirements for tensor product mappings and analyzing geometric structures like principal bundles over state spaces.
model_or_system: The focus is on abstract Quantum Theory (QT) foundations, specifically dealing with observables (Hermitian operators), state spaces ($K$), effect spaces ($L$), and the composition of systems via Hilbert space tensor products in the finite-dimensional limit.
key_observables: Observables are Hermitian operators; key diagnostics include the structure of product states and the existence/choice of 'quantum orientation'.
important_parameters: The analysis is strictly limited to the finite-dimensional case ($	ext{dim}(H)=N$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the statistical structure alone is insufficient, necessitating the introduction of the Noether structure; the analysis also assumes specific mappings related to tensor products.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying the insufficiency of the statistical structure, then investigating composition via tensor products, leading to the discovery of non-uniqueness in composite structures. It concludes with detailed mathematical proofs concerning homeomorphisms between state space descriptions and the characterization of pure operations.
why_interesting: This work tackles foundational issues regarding how quantum theories must be mathematically structured when combining subsystems or defining irreversible processes (operations), which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems dynamics.
